newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB raises most December 96/97 wheat PROs.
newsitem.headline: CWB raises most December 96/97 wheat PROs.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board raised its December Pool Return Outlook in most wheat grade price forecasts for the 1996/97 (August/July) crop year by C$5 a tonne and durum wheat by C$6 a tonne but dropped malt barley by C$3, a CWB release stated.
The PROs are a monthly Board estimate of world prices but not connected to CWB initial payments to farmers.
The benchmark No1 Canada Western Red Spring Wheat PRO was not changed from the C$194-C$214 range.
No1 Canada Western Amber Durum wheat rose C$6 a tonne to the C$208-228 range from C$203-233.
No1 Canada Western Feed Barley was unchanged from the C$140-C$160 range in November.
Special select Canada Western Two-Row Malting Barley prices fell to C$217-C$237 from the C$220-C$240 range. Special select Canada Western Six-Row Malt barley fell to C$177-C$197 from C$180-C$200.

The CWB said rain in Argentina delayed the wheat harvest and lead to quality concerns. Rain there and steady import demand increased global values for mid-quality wheat. The current cold weather in the United States hard red winter wheat zone has potential for winter kill, the CWB said.
Durum wheat prices rose on steady import demand, the CWB said.
Malt barley crop prospects in Australia remained favorable and high selection rates were anticipated. The large EU barley crop and high export subsidies continued to weigh on malt barley values.
Pool returns in Canadian dollars per tonne based on grain in store St. Lawrence or Vancouver:
CWF=Canada Western Feed. CWAD=Canada Western Amber Durum.
